findings.hypothesis: A very large group (4,267) started a booking but never chose a slot and therefore never reached confirmation; this single segment alone explains most of the 4,804 lost bookings between started and confirmed.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab 'no_slot_chosen' with clickstream events to see whether these sessions reached the slot-selection UI or the payments page; instrument a small UI change that forces an explicit slot selection before proceeding and measure lift in confirmed bookings vs holdout.

segments: users who returned from the payments page
findings.hypothesis: Independent of the 'no_slot_chosen' group, payment-page abandonment is a major driver: 3,520 recorded cases of customers going back from the payments page match the large created->confirmed gap and point to payment failures, confusion or friction at checkout.
findings.confirm_via: Add instrumentation to mark a 'visited payments page' event and capture payment-provider error codes; cross-tab those events with app version, interface_type and transaction_source to identify whether abandonment is due to provider errors, UI timeouts or user choice, then run a recovery experiment that surfaces clearer error messaging and one-tap retry.

findings.hypothesis: Consumer flows account for most volume and convert much worse than corporate channels: the main consumer channel 'halodoc_customer' converted 652 of 5,193 (12.56%) and b2c converted 993 of 5,777 (17.19%), so most of the lost bookings live in consumer UX/payment paths rather than corporate onboarding.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab transaction_source and target_market with 'visited payments page' and with abandon_reason to see whether the consumer drop is concentrated at payments; run a targeted simplified-payment experiment for halodoc_customer users (e.g., saved payment UI) and compare confirmed bookings to a control group.

findings.hypothesis: Android sessions convert worse (223 of 2,164 = 10.3%) than iOS (515 of 3,293 = 15.64%); this suggests a platform-specific payments/checkout issue affecting a meaningful portion of consumer volume.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab Android sessions with payment-provider logs and Play Store error reports, reproduce checkout on the lowest-converting Android builds, and A/B test an alternate checkout flow (e.g., webview or external browser) for Android to measure impact.

segments: several regional markets (East Java, Central Java, Sumatera)
findings.hypothesis: A small number of regions show very low conversion (e.g., East Java 10 of 187 = 5.35%); these could be caused by local payment provider issues, telco instability, or supply-side availability in those markets, but their total entered counts are modest so they explain only a small fraction of the overall loss.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab region with 'visited payments page', payment-provider response codes and provider availability; run a local diagnostic and a region-specific fallback payment method pilot to measure lift.

growth_ideas.title: One-tap saved payments
growth_ideas.rationale: Consumer bookings (halodoc_customer) have low conversion (12.56%); reducing payment friction for returning consumers should convert more of that large volume.
growth_ideas.description: Let returning consumers securely save a single default payment method and enable a one-tap 'pay and confirm' button on checkout so repeat bookings skip manual card entry; include explicit consent and a simple revoke button in profile settings.

growth_ideas.title: 10-minute slot hold
growth_ideas.rationale: Many users start bookings but never choose a slot (4,267); a short hold removes time pressure and lets users pick a slot and finish payment without losing availability.
growth_ideas.description: Allow users to reserve a specific slot for 10 minutes without immediate payment; show an in-app countdown and send a push/SMS reminder with a one-tap payment link before the hold expires.

growth_ideas.title: Payment-failure recovery flow
growth_ideas.rationale: 3,520 recorded cases of users returning from the payments page indicate many checkouts fail or confuse users; a recovery flow should reclaim a large share of these abandonments.
growth_ideas.description: When a payment attempt fails or the user navigates away from payment, show an immediate in-app diagnostic explaining the error and offer two alternatives: retry payment with one tap, or complete checkout via WhatsApp/web checkout pre-filled with booking details; log provider error codes for analytics.

growth_ideas.title: WhatsApp fallback checkout
growth_ideas.rationale: WhatsApp-originated bookings convert far better (70.06%) than the main consumer channel; offering a WhatsApp checkout fallback for users who hit errors can recover successful transactions quickly.
growth_ideas.description: If a consumer's in-app payment fails (especially on Android), surface a one-tap option to continue checkout through a WhatsApp flow with pre-filled booking details and a payment link or agent-assisted checkout.
